neighbours.label: money words: ' sh' of shilling and ' cash' (a coin or cash sum being paid)
fire: He spent a shilling on a copy of the lord keeper's speech.
The rent was set at one English shilling a year.
She paid for the groceries in cash at the corner shop.
In 1380 a tax of one shilling a head was granted.
The thieves took all the cash from the till.
A loaf of bread cost a shilling in those days.
They offered him cash for the old car.
The boy earned a shilling for carrying the bags.
quiet: He spent an hour reading the lord keeper's speech.
The rent was set once a year by the landlord.
She paid for the groceries with her card at the corner shop.
In 1380 a new tax on every household was granted.
The thieves took all the jewels from the safe.
A loaf of bread was baked every morning in those days.
They offered him a ride in the old car.
The boy got a smile for carrying the bags.
